parts:
Hi.

On Thu, Jul 23, 2009 at 4:50 AM, Stellaw Chao<stella...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi Henrik,
> Much thanks!I have tried "extractMatrix" and it works!
>
> Yet another question merges...I used RMAExpress to extract the
> expression level matrix some time ago (background adjusted, quantile
> normalized and summarized using PLM) . I thought the outcomes of these
> two preprocessing softwares (namely RMAExpress and aroma.affymetrix)
> ought to be the same, yet they are not ...

Differences occur because although the models for each of the
different preprocessing steps are rather much the same, their
estimators (algorithms) differ. For instance, there are many
different ways to do quantile normalization and to fit the
log-additive model. Having said this, various group members have try
to understand the differences in more detail and show how to reproduce
some existing methods. In Vignette 'Reproducibility of other
implementations' it is shown how to reproduce RMA according
Biconductor's affyPLM (Ben Bolstad):

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/redundancy-tests

>
> I asked my mentor about this question of "inconsistency", and showed
> him the "aroma.affymetrix-Analysis of small to very large Affymetrix
> data sets"(which is written by you in August, 2007 =D).

It took me a while to figure out which you one meant; it's the slides
used in my BioC2007 lab:

Henrik Bengtsson, aroma.affymetrix - Analysis of small to very large
Affymetrix data sets, Bioconductor Workshop, Seattle, August 7, 2007
http://www.bioconductor.org/workshops/2007/BioC2007/labs/aroma/

FYI, although I try to have a stable design, 2007 is a very long time
ago in our area. I recommend you to use more recent documentation
available on the group page.

>
> He saw the descripton on page 48 that "# The SNP information contains
> information about SNP fragment lengths.
> cdf <- getCdf(ces)
> si <-getSnpInformation(cdf)
> fl <- getFragmentLengths(si)" and doubted whether I am using the right
> software since the dataset I am currently working with measures the
> DNA expression level.

The aroma.affymetrix package can analyze pretty much all Affymetrix
chip types, but you mentor is correct that you do not want to DNA copy
analysis, but rather RNA expression analysis. Instead, see the
several of the vignettes and example online:

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web

Cheers,

/Henrik
